description.narrative:
Somalia is experiencing its fifth continuous unsuccessful rainy season by mid-2023. According to the FSNAU report of Dec 13, 2023.,nearly 8.3 million people across Somalia face Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse acute food insecurity outcomes It is predicted that there will be a sixth season of below-average rainfall from March to June 2023, and extraordinarily high food costs, compounded by ongoing conflict/insecurity and disease outbreaks resulting in an unparalleled level of need within Somalia.
Furthermore, an increasing number of people are likely to be in Catastrophe (IPC Phase 5) in a variety of different places across Somalia until mid-2023. Theresults of previous integrated surveys conducted between May and July 2022, as well as the subsequent IPC acute malnutrition analysis reported on Dec 13, 2023, remain valid, with the total estimated acute malnutrition burden in Somalia reaching approximately 1.8 million children through July 2023, including 513,550 children who are likely to be severely malnourished . Overall, the situation remains extremely serious as the underlying crisis has not improved and the scope and severity of the humanitarian disaster are growing. Famine is a real threat from April to June 2023 and beyond if humanitarian assistance is not maintained and if rainfall is projected in 2023. As famine (IPC Phase 5) is projected among agropastoral communities in the Baidoa and Burhakaba districts of the Bay region, as well as among internally displaced people (IDP) in Baidoa town and in Mogadishu, between April and June 2023, ARC Replica is targeting the Bay region and the two most affected districts. These three locations already have extremely high levels of acute malnutrition and death, which corresponds to the Emergency (IPC Phase 4) phase.
